---
title: "A files view: synced folders you can browse"
date: 2026-11-27
lang: en
---

The idea (user, 2026-11-27): a **files** section, like devices, where you choose which
folders sync, and browse their files: select them, open them, drag files in.

What Joma has today: folder sync runs on Joma's own Syncthing over Jami tunnels
(0.5.2.dev12, design note 08). Folders are added in devices → synced folders or with
`joma sync add <path>`; the list shows each folder's state. Received files land in
`~/Downloads/joma`. GPUI (Joma's toolkit) takes files dropped from other apps, but it
cannot start a drag towards other apps on Linux: it uses the Wayland data source only
for the clipboard (checked in gpui 0.2.2).

Sketch: a seventh icon in the rail, **files** (Ctrl+7). The list on the left holds the
synced folders (with their state) and, below, **received** (files from conversations).
The right side browses the chosen folder: a path line, rows with icon, name, size,
modified and sync state, a preview for pictures, voice and video (Joma's own viewer and
player). Synced-folder settings move from devices to here; devices keeps a short line
("2 folders synced").

# 1. Where it lives

A new rail entry **files**, between devices and accounts. Proposal: yes; devices keeps
only a count that links here.

- [x] A:

# 2. What it shows

Synced folders only, or also files from conversations? Proposal: synced folders, then a
**received** group: every file of every conversation that is on this machine (from who,
when, a click opens the message). One place to find "that PDF Marta sent".

- [x] A: conversations should get their folder. e.g. i send files to a group chat, there is a folder for the others that accept the files. now. if someone else delete the file on their device, the file stays in the folder but unsynced for them. so in conversations, the default is read-only for members and edit for whom shared the file.
  however this can be configured, as we can do for a normal shared folder. so we can treat the conversations folders (let's have a nice folder structure for these) as normal shared folders for joma. where the admin of the group can set admins, and set permissions, e.g. who reads/writes (users or everybody). this way we can have group chats that become working groups. and also documents can be edited by multiple people working together in the same group chat. we then have one model for shared folders. the main difference is that when we create a shared folder we get to decide which folder we share (or one from joma shared folder with a suggested name...) while in a conversation, as soon as we drop files they go in  a shared folder. video and audio messages, should also go in there in sub-folders as they are not documents. a conversation might have a set of defined sub-folders e.g. images, gifs, audio, video, documents so most of the files would be put in the right spot, where audio and video would also contain the messages subfolders with the audio and video messages

# 3. Choosing what syncs, per device

Today a folder goes to all your devices. Syncthing can share a folder with some devices
only. Proposal: each folder lists your devices with a switch each (default: all that run
Joma); a new device gets the folders marked "all devices".

- [x] A:

# 4. Browsing and selecting

Proposal: click selects, Ctrl/Shift+click adds, Enter or double click opens with the
system's app (`xdg-open`), Space previews in Joma, Delete moves to the trash (Syncthing
passes the deletion on, so it asks first and says on how many devices). Keys like the
chat list (j/k, /).

- [x] A:

# 5. Drag and drop

Into Joma: dropping files on a folder copies them in (Shift: move); dropping on a
conversation sends them, as today. From the browser onto a conversation in Joma: sends
(an internal drag, works). Out of Joma into other apps: GPUI cannot start it. Options:
(a) a **copy** action that puts the files on the clipboard as file paths (most file
managers and browsers take a paste); (b) "show in folder" opens the system file
manager there; (c) a small helper (`ripdrag`, AUR) started for the selected files,
which other apps can drag from. Proposal: (a) and (b) now, (c) only if you miss real
dragging.

- [x] A: show in folder is fine, and on a folder "open in file manager..." something like that

# 6. Conflicts and old versions

When two devices change a file at once, Syncthing keeps both (`name.sync-conflict-…`).
It can also keep old versions of changed and deleted files. Proposal: conflicts show as
a badge on the file with "keep this / keep the other"; folders keep old versions for 30
days (Syncthing's "staggered" versioning) under the folder's `.stversions`, browsable
from the file's menu.

- [x] A:

# 7. The phone

Joma for Android has no Syncthing yet. Proposal: later, as its own discussion: browsing
a home device's folder from the phone over a Jami tunnel (no full copy on the phone) is
a better fit than syncing everything.

- [x] A: yes, we do not sync to phones. as long as the phone can see the folder content and download what it needs on demand, that's perfect

# 8. Commands

Proposal, like the other features: `joma files` (folders and their state),
`joma files ls <folder> [path] [--json]`, `joma files open <path>`, `joma sync share
<folder> <device>|--all` for question 3.

- [x] A:

## Built (2026-11-28, 0.5.3.dev4 to dev8)

The files view (Ctrl+7) with offers, your folders, folders shared with people,
conversations and received files; one model for shared folders (owner, members who read
or write, admins, everybody writes); a conversation's files as one folder per member,
sorted into images, gifs, audio (and audio/messages), video (and video/messages) and
documents; open, show in folder, open in file manager, copy path, delete to the trash;
conflicts with keep this / keep the other; old versions 30 days. Not yet: the keys of
question 4 (j/k, Space to preview), browsing from the phone (question 7).
